description.narrative:
The overall purpose of the eSpace reform is to integrate all national digital registers important for the place-based approach (based on geospatial location and related data) to sustainable development, and to provide access to data and services when, where and how citizens, businesses and public bodies may need them.
The expected outcomes of the proposed project are the following: Outcome 1: RGA has developed a strategic action plan, established cooperation with stakeholders at central and local government level, and developed capacity to lead the establishment of the ePlan system. Outcome 2: A Pilot database with verified digitalization tools, methodologies, and pilot data for responding to the INSPIRE Directive obligation and SDGs integration in the area of land use planning and management that is made available for all stakeholders. Outcome 3: A Pilot database with verified digitalisation tools, methodology and pilot data for storing and accessing information on legal regimes for land use planning and development is developed and functional. Outcome 4: Organizational structure for ePlan system implementation is established, all stakeholders (government institutions at central and local level) are informed and aware about ePlan system benefits for participatory and transparent sustainable development.

Projektet sträcker sig över tre år (2022-2025) med det övergripande målet att stödja utvecklingen av en modern datahanteringsstandard och kapacitetsbyggande aktiviteter för fysisk, urban och hållbar planering i Serbien. Detta stöd är ämnat att lägga grunden för en mer effektiv, transparent och deltagande styrningsmodell. Implementeringen av projektet kommer ske genom samarbete mellan de serbiska och svenska myndigheterna RGA och Lantmäteriet.

The project is a three-year intervention (2022-2025) with the overall goal to support development of a modern data management standards and capacity building activities for spatial and urban plans and sustainable planning in Serbia. Support provided within this contribution is expected to lay the foundation for a more efficient, effective, transparent, and participatory governance model. The contribution will be implemented in cooperation between Serbian and Swedish authorities: RGA and Lantmäteriet.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
Progress of the project can be summarized in the following way: Outcome 1 During 2025, RGA implemented planned activities related to the application and maintenance of ISO 37001 (Anti Bribery Management System). The activities were aimed at strengthening institutional capacities, enhancing employees knowledge and awareness, and ensuring consistent and effective implementation of the standard. The project has supported the audit review of the ISO 37001 anti corruption certification. Having this ISO certification as a basis, the trust from citizens are increasing and people feel more confident using the transparent services provided by RGA.
Outcome 2 Component Establishment of the Smart Parcel system The outputs created during 2025 present the significant step towards the achievement of this Components goals and, thus, accomplishment of the overall SmartSDI projects aim, by improving the NSDI capacities and its stakeholders capabilities and capacities to use the geospatial data and services for the sustainable development decision making and policies management. The key project stakeholders of the system include citizens, businesses, municipalities/cities, and other public sector entities. The current status of the SmartParcel system is that it is established and has been piloted. Currently, several data owners (municipalities/cities and state insitutions) are entering data and additional stakeholders are introduced. Once the data are available, the SmartParcel system gives them open, transparent and easy access to planning documents and related data, including planned land use for each specific location. This includes direct access to information and insights on what is planned and when development is expected. They will be able to see how investments are envisaged and their anticipated environmental impacts. In this way, the system supports location based, data driven decision making at all levels. Through the SmartParcel system, the data made available online is supporting more efficient service delivery, faster response times and better alignment with the needs and preferences of citizens and businesses. As data is stored and maintained in standardized formats, they can be integrated with other datasets across the NSDI. This will facilitate more effective communication, cooperation, and data sharing across sectors at both national and local levels. The system will support EU Cohesion Policy implementation in Serbia and coordination of European and national investment instruments needed for green transition, contributing to Serbia's accession to the European Union.
Outcomes 2 Component National database for Planned Land Use (PLU) established in accordance with the INSPIRE Directive In cooperation with 18 pilot local governments in the Republic of Serbia an initial national database with the geospatial data on Planned Land Use database (PLU) was established in accordance with requirements of the European INSPIRE Directive for the Land Use theme. By creating and integrating the PLU database with other standardized geospatial data within the NSDI Infrastructure of the Republic of Serbia, the initial conditions have been created for further digitalization of the spatial and urban planning system.
Outcomes 2 Component Validation of the EUREF Serbia 2023 Campaign Improvements of the Geodetic Infrastructure, aimed to at enhance the national geospatial infrastructure and ensuring compliance with European standards, RGA received expert support from Lantmäteriet in data processing and in the preparation of the national report for the EUREF Serbia 2023 campaign. As part of these project activities, the RGA submitted the national report of the Republic of Serbia entitled EUREF Serbia 2023 to the EUREF Governing Board (EUREF International Association of Geodesy, Reference Frame Sub Commission for Europe) for validation. The EUREF Governing Board confirmed the results of the campaign carried out by the RGA Geo Sector. The campaign results were presented to the wider EUREF community at the EUREF 2025 Symposium, held in Covilhã, Portugal. The official confirmation of the campaign through an EUREF Resolution is expected at the EUREF 2026 Symposium in Paris, France.
Outcomes 3; Component Establishing Portfolio Management and Project Planning Support for SmartSDI Building A better way of organizing and managing projects helps ensure that public money is used more efficiently and transparently, while also strengthening RGA as an institution. Through this project RGA introduced a simple but efficient system for managing its projects, allowing better control of time, budget and staff. This also helps RGA build internal capacity to plan, implement and monitor projects more effectively. Managers can now clearly see what is happening, detect problems early, and react before delays or overspending occur. It was developed by the project in close cooperation with RGA and has been piloted for several projects. It is now accepted and taken over by RGA. as a basis for further development and upscaled implementation.
Outcome 4; Component Stakeholders capacity building, engagement and communication 74 municipalities were actively involved in the project to verify that the solutions being developed meet their local needs. By participating in surveys, discussions, and pilot activities, municipalities were able to share their needs and challenges, to help shape the SmartParcel system into the tool they need. This means the final solution is very useful in their daily work, enabling the municipalities to make better decisions and provide better services.
Outcome 4 Component Delivery of e-learning distribution platform An e-learning distribution platform was successfully delivered. The platform provides structured access to educational video content for both citizens and professional users, with the objective of supporting and promoting the use of digital services of RGA. This has resulted in information being available online more easily for citizens, companies, and local governments. They can learn how to use services through short videos, and complete tasks faster without going to a physical office and reducing the need for additional customer support. This is saving time and money for both users and RGA.
Outcome 4 Component Establishment of a webstudio During 2025 project efforts was put on improving accessibility of information for external stakeholders, such as municiapalities and cities. In this context, the introduction of a Webstudio is an important step towards more open, transparent and efficient communication. This helps everyone stay informed about what the RGA is doing, why it matters, and how it affects them. The web studio will enable RGA to present its activities, services, and data in a clear, engaging and interactive way to a wider audience. The webstudio will enable several ways for communication, such as webinars, online trainings and podcasts. Instead of being forced to searching through complicated documents, people will be able to watch instruction videos or listen to short podcasts and find the information they need. This makes communication more open, interactive and transparent. It also reduces confusion, and helps people trust the information they receive thereby increasing the trust for RGA. Using current achievements of this projects, but also plans and projections for the coming years, RGA is working closely with a handful of other institutions who are seen as relevant partners and users of data produced by RGA. Some of those institutions are: Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Construction and Civil Engineering, Ministry of Interior/Department for Disaster Risk Reduction, Agency for Spatial Planning and others. The Agency for Spatial Planning is also partner of NALED (other Sida funded project). The two institutions (RGA and the Agency) as well as the two contributions are coordinated by the partners with limited Sida's involvement.
